customManagers.description: Tag-pinned deps in the DEFAULTS block of the ledger (deps.json). JSONata reads the parsed document, so the ledger's key order and any extra fields (reason, registryUrl, ...) no longer matter -- the regex managers this replaced required origin/tag/datasource to be contiguous and in order, and a harmless reorder silently dropped a dep from tracking. Only .defaults is queried; .overrides (per-version / per-platform holds) is never touched. A dep is tracked iff it has a `tag` AND a `datasource` key: the datasource VALUE is informational (all git hosts are queried uniformly through git-tags against the clone URL, which is also what the packageRules below match on), its PRESENCE is the opt-in. Commit pins and tarball deps are handled by the two managers below, so every ledger dep is tracked by exactly one manager -- asserted by scripts/ci/renovate-coverage-test.sh.

Deps pinned to a reviewed commit rather than a tag (x264 publishes no release tags; the Vulkan shim has no releases). Tracked as git-refs digests against the branch the pin actually follows: the key is digestBranch, NOT branch, because the ledger treats tag/branch/commit as mutually exclusive ref types (scripts/deps/lib.sh picks the first one present), so a second ref key would fail ledger-validate and could change which ref gets built.

Deps that ship as a plain tarball with no git remote (GNU FTP, SourceForge, quut.com): versions come from the upstream release listing via the html custom datasource, selected by a `releasesUrl` key. The extractVersion is anchored to each project's OWN artifact name -- an html listing exposes every link on the page, so a shape-only pattern would accept an unrelated project's archive on a shared listing (SourceForge hosts opencore-amr and vo-amrwbenc under one project). The per-dep patterns live in the $lookup table here; a tarball dep missing from it yields no extractVersion, which renovate-coverage-test.sh fails on rather than letting Renovate treat every link as a version. Numeric-dot only: 'loose' records a trailing suffix as suffix rather than prerelease, so a future 3.102beta would otherwise rank as stable. [.] rather than \. in the patterns because JSONata string literals reject that escape.

FFmpeg point releases: one entry per maintained major line in the .ffmpeg array of deps.json (e.g. 8.1.2). FFmpeg's upstream tags are n<version>, stripped via extractVersion. The per-major packageRules below keep each line inside its own major.

Pinning the ACTION (renovatebot/github-action) does not pin Renovate itself: the action's default renovate-version pulls a moving major tag, so the tool that maintains every other pin was itself unpinned and untracked. renovate.yml pins a full version and this manager keeps it updated from the published container tags.

Build/test container images (issue #26). The musl, glibc and armhf builds run inside these images, so the image IS the toolchain: a floating alpine:latest or untagged manylinux ref changed GCC/musl/glibc between runs with no diff on our side. Every ref in build.yml/test.yml is pinned tag@sha256 and tracked here; scripts/ci/image-pins-test.sh asserts none is left unpinned or unmatched. Tag and digest are captured separately so Renovate can bump either -- bookworm only ever moves its digest.

packageRules.description: Group all ledger dependency bumps under a clear prefix so CI (build + docs-matrix) validates each PR against every FFmpeg line before merge.

Batch EVERY ledger update -- major, minor, patch and digest alike -- into ONE grouped PR per run. Majors used to be left ungrouped so each got individual scrutiny, but every one of these updates edits deps.json, so concurrent PRs conflict with each other and the conflict resolution costs more than the separate review buys. One PR means one deps.json to reason about and one CI run (build + docs-matrix) validating the whole set against every FFmpeg line. A major that needs to be held back can be split out by pinning it in .overrides with a tracking issue.

Anything pinned INSIDE a workflow file (renovate-version; the build/test container images are split further into their own group by the next rule) gets its OWN PR, separate from the ledger group above. Renovate cannot push to .github/workflows/ unless its token carries the workflow scope, and when it cannot it does not skip that one file -- it logs 'Workflows update rejection - aborting branch' and discards the ENTIRE branch, so a single un-writable file silently took out every library bump in the batch (measured: vmaf, whisper.cpp, shaderc and libmp3lame updates were all dropped while the job still reported success). Splitting by file keeps the blast radius of a missing scope to this PR alone, and the ledger keeps flowing regardless. Matched by file rather than by dep name so a future workflow pin lands here automatically.

Build/test container images in their OWN PR, after the ledger group above so it wins. Same reason as Renovate itself: these refs live in .github/workflows/, and a token without the workflow scope aborts the whole branch, so they must not ride in the ledger batch. A merged bump rebuilds and releases every FFmpeg line (select-versions.sh keys on the changed @sha256 line), so this is one PR Renovate keeps rebased rather than one per image: merge it at the cadence a toolchain change deserves.

manylinux publishes date tags (YYYY.MM.DD-N, N = same-day rebuild). Default docker versioning reads the -N suffix as a compatibility marker rather than an ordinal, so spell the scheme out: build orders same-day rebuilds.

Alpine: offer patch and minor releases (3.24.x -> 3.25.y) -- a minor IS a new GCC/musl and therefore a new ABI floor for the musl artifacts, which is exactly why it must arrive as a reviewable PR rather than silently. Never the edge/date-tagged development stream.

Vulkan-Headers/Loader + SPIRV-Headers ship in lockstep on vulkan-sdk-* release tags (the ledger pins the same SDK version across all three). Each repo ALSO carries a parallel v1.4.x tag scheme; restrict Renovate to the vulkan-sdk-* versioning so it can't cross namespaces or desync the trio (which it otherwise would — it proposed v1.4.360 for Loader+SPIRV but not Headers).

Constrain each FFmpeg line to its own MAJOR: Renovate offers any newer release within the major — patch or minor alike (9.0.1 -> 9.0.2 -> 9.1.0) — but never a cross-major jump (9.x -> 10.x). One rule per maintained major; matchCurrentVersion scopes it to the line at that major, allowedVersions filters candidates to that major. A NEW major is a new line that check-updates.yml adds (with its matching rule).

Hold mbedTLS on 3.x. mbedTLS 4.x removed <mbedtls/ctr_drbg.h> and <mbedtls/entropy.h> when that work moved to PSA Crypto (the TF-PSA-Crypto split). Its consumers here are SRT and librist -- FFmpeg's own TLS layer uses OpenSSL/GnuTLS/SChannel in this build -- so the hold lifts when the SRT and librist versions we ship support 4.x. Without this the grouped PR would carry a bump nothing has validated. The rationale, tracking issue (#18) and review date live in deps.json (.defaults.mbedtls.hold); scripts/ci/holds-test.sh keeps this rule and that record in step.

Hold nv-codec-headers on the SDK 13.0 line: sdk/13.1 raises the minimum NVIDIA driver to 610, which Maxwell/Pascal/Volta cards (last driver: 580) can never run, and FFmpeg's NVENC refuses to open on an older driver. 13.0.x patch releases still flow. The rationale, tracking issue and review date live in deps.json (.defaults["nv-codec"].hold) -- metadata keys here would make Renovate refuse to start (see renovate-config-test.sh) -- and scripts/ci/holds-test.sh keeps this rule and that record in step. versioning: tags are n<major>.<minor>.<patch>.<build>, and the default semver-coerced scheme drops the fourth component, so n13.0.19.1 -> n13.0.19.2 would never compare as newer.

tarball-listing.description: Upstream release listing for deps that ship as a plain tarball with no git remote (GNU FTP, SourceForge, quut.com). format:html makes Renovate return every <a href> on the page verbatim; the manager's extractVersion then pulls the version out of whichever shape that site uses.
